description:
Episode 101 of a daily journey through the universe. 🪐
We explore super-Earths: planets bigger than Earth but smaller than Neptune, the most common kind found around other stars, missing from our own solar system, from lava worlds like 55 Cancri e to possible water worlds.

segments.text: Episode one hundred and one. Next stop... super-Earths.
We've found more than six thousand planets around other stars. And the most common size surprised everyone.
Planets bigger than Earth, but smaller than Neptune. We call the rocky ones super-Earths.
segments.headline: Bigger than Earth

segments.text: Our solar system doesn't have a single one. Nobody knows exactly why.
segments.headline: We don't have one

segments.text: Some are lava worlds. Like fifty-five Cancri e, so hot its surface may be melted rock.
segments.headline: Lava worlds

segments.text: In twenty twenty-four, the Webb telescope found signs that fifty-five Cancri e has an atmosphere, maybe bubbling out of its magma.
segments.headline: Webb takes a look

segments.text: Others might be water worlds, covered by a single ocean hundreds of kilometers deep.
segments.headline: Water worlds

segments.text: With stronger gravity, a super-Earth could hold a thick atmosphere, and maybe taller waves and flatter mountains.
Some of the best places to look for life beyond Earth might be super-Earths.
segments.headline: Life on a super-Earth?

segments.text: Tomorrow is a sky event. A lunar eclipse so faint, most people won't notice it. Can you? Follow, so you don't miss episode one hundred and two.
